features.name: molecular_complexity_ratio
features.description: Ratio of aromatic/ring-related descriptors (V16) to total atom count proxy (V10 + V11 + 1), capturing structural complexity relative to size
features.expected_model_benefit: Tree splits on this ratio can separate simple vs complex molecular structures that differ in biodegradability

features.name: polarity_asymmetry
features.description: Absolute difference between two electronegativity/polarity descriptors V17 and V18, indicating molecular polarity imbalance
features.expected_model_benefit: Polarity asymmetry can indicate susceptibility to enzymatic attack, relevant to biodegradation

features.name: heteroatom_density
features.description: Sum of nitrogen/oxygen-related counts (V3 + V4 + V5 + V6) normalized by molecular size proxy V8, representing heteroatom density
features.expected_model_benefit: Higher heteroatom density often correlates with biodegradability due to functional group availability

features.name: log_molecular_weight_proxy
features.description: Log-transformed molecular weight proxy V8, compressing the skewed distribution for better tree splits
features.expected_model_benefit: Log transformation reveals nonlinear size thresholds that trees can exploit for biodegradation prediction

features.name: branching_indicator
features.description: Boolean indicator for high branching: V7 (branching count) exceeds 2, indicating highly branched structures
features.expected_model_benefit: Branched molecules often resist biodegradation; binary split enables direct tree node separation

features.name: lipophilicity_polarity_interaction
features.description: Product of lipophilicity proxy V1 and polarity descriptor V22, capturing the interaction between hydrophobicity and polarity
features.expected_model_benefit: Nonlinear interaction between lipophilicity and polarity is a known driver of biodegradation; trees can split on this product

features.name: charge_deviation_from_neutral
features.description: Absolute value of V12 (charge-related descriptor), measuring deviation from neutral charge state
features.expected_model_benefit: Charged molecules behave differently in biological systems; absolute charge deviation enables threshold splits

features.name: ring_system_complexity_bucket
features.description: Ordinal bucket for ring system complexity based on V16: 0=no rings, 1=low (1-3), 2=medium (4-8), 3=high (>8)
features.expected_model_benefit: Ordinal ring complexity buckets provide direct categorical splits for tree models on structural features

features.name: functional_group_richness
features.description: Count of diverse functional group indicators: sum of binary/low-count descriptors V19, V24, V25, V26, V29 indicating presence of special functional groups
features.expected_model_benefit: Molecules with more diverse functional groups tend to be more biodegradable; count enables ordinal splits

features.name: size_normalized_connectivity
features.description: Ratio of connectivity descriptor V31 to molecular size proxy V8, capturing connectivity density
features.expected_model_benefit: Connectivity per unit size captures molecular graph density, which influences biodegradation pathways

features.name: aromatic_fraction_estimate
features.description: Estimated fraction of aromatic character based on V16 (aromatic ring count) relative to V10 (total ring-related atoms). Score from 0 (fully aliphatic) to 1 (highly aromatic). Aromatic compounds are generally less biodegradable.
features.expected_model_benefit: Aromatic fraction is a key predictor of biodegradation resistance; provides a continuous score for tree splits

features.name: molecular_flexibility_score
features.description: Interaction of rotatable bond proxy V9 and chain length proxy V34, measuring overall molecular flexibility as product clipped to reasonable range
features.expected_model_benefit: Flexible molecules with long chains are more accessible to enzymatic degradation; nonlinear interaction enables tree splits
